notes: Each run gets its own copy of the config so the live config is never mutated. Runs are graded on outputs/response.md and outputs/changes.diff.

evals.name: audit-drift-report
evals.prompt: been hacking on this nvim config for months and it's definitely drifted. can you go through it and tell me what's inconsistent?
evals.expected_output: An inline report grouped by severity, citing real drift with file:line. Should spare the deliberate exceptions and should not edit files without asking.
assertions: Reports mixed tab/space indentation in at least 3 of the 4 genuinely-mixed files (config/lsp.lua, config/options.lua, plugins/dashboard.lua, plugins/vim-dadbod.lua)
Reports that plugins/dashboard.lua has no header comment
Flags the <leader>tt or <leader>tb toggle desc naming inconsistency
Cites concrete file paths for findings rather than only general prose
Groups findings by severity or priority rather than presenting one flat list
Does NOT claim vim-helm.lua is buggy for lacking once = true (it deletes its own augroup, which is correct there)
Does NOT propose deleting a lua/plugins/*.lua file as dead code
Does NOT propose alphabetising or reordering pack.lua / init.lua
Made no edits to the config (changes.diff is empty)

evals.name: add-plugin-registration
evals.prompt: add nvim-surround, i want to be able to change quotes and brackets around things
evals.expected_output: All three registration points updated, house style matched, and crucially not a lazy.nvim spec.
assertions: Adds an nvim-surround entry to the vim.pack.add list in lua/pack.lua
Creates lua/plugins/nvim-surround.lua
Adds a require("plugins.nvim-surround") line to init.lua
All three registration points are present (the full triangle)
Contains NO lazy.nvim spec vocabulary (a returned table using opts/event/cmd/ft/keys/dependencies)
Calls require("nvim-surround").setup(...)
New plugin file opens with the two-line header: name and description, then the GitHub URL
New plugin file is tab-indented

evals.name: filetype-scoped-keymap
evals.prompt: i work in a lot of .sql files — i want <leader>Dr to run the current file against my dev db via dadbod, but only in sql buffers
evals.expected_output: A buffer-local keymap in lua/plugins/vim-dadbod.lua, scoped to sql via a FileType autocmd, with a desc. House rule: plugin ownership beats filetype scoping, so this does NOT belong in after/ftplugin/sql.lua.
assertions: Places the keymap in lua/plugins/vim-dadbod.lua (plugin owns its keymaps)
Does NOT put a plugin keymap in after/ftplugin/sql.lua
Maps <leader>Dr specifically
Keymap is scoped to sql buffers (buffer-local, not global)
Keymap includes a desc
Does NOT add a global keymap in lua/config/keymaps.lua
Does NOT add a FileType autocmd in lua/config/autocmds.lua to achieve this
